haiku-low.q1: Reserved for 10 minutes. If not claimed in time, the expiry job sets the hold EXPIRED and returns the stock to sale.
haiku-low.q2: Before the charge. If any line is short, nothing is reserved, no payment is requested, and the reply lists the short items. Cart is untouched.
haiku-low.q3: The charge uses the order id as idempotency key, and retries reuse the same key, so the provider cannot charge twice.
haiku-low.q4: Order cancels as out of stock, emails the customer, and publishes RefundRequested. Payment refunds the full amount. Cart is untouched.
haiku-low.q5: Cart removes only the ordered lines, when OrderConfirmed arrives, in one transaction. If checkout fails, the cart is left exactly as it was.
haiku-low.q6: The Order service moves each checkout forward. Its orders table status, with status_changed_at, records how far each checkout has got.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment, which verifies its signature, saves the outcome, and publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentFailed to Order.
haiku-low.q8: Payment saves each provider event id in a unique-keyed table in the same transaction; repeats are ignored with 200. Order also ignores events by current status.
haiku-low.q9: Payment declined: Order marks it PAYMENT_DECLINED and publishes OrderFailed. Inventory releases the hold, setting RELEASED, if it is still RESERVED.
haiku-low.q10: Inventory claims if the hold is RESERVED, or EXPIRED but every line is still available. Otherwise it refuses, and Order cancels and refunds.
haiku-low.q11: The refund row stays PENDING in Payment's refunds table, and the refund scheduler retries with backoff. After N failures: REFUND_FAILED, ops alerted, retries continue.
haiku-low.q12: Order publishing OrderConfirmed causes Cart to remove the ordered lines. Cart service does this, in one transaction, and only for the ordered quantities.

sonnet.q1: Held 10 minutes. If not claimed, the expiry job (I3, runs about every 30 s) sets the reservation EXPIRED (only if still RESERVED) and returns the stock to sale. A late claim can still succeed if every line is still free.
sonnet.q2: Stock is reserved before the charge (payment is requested only after the reservation succeeds). If any line is short, nothing is reserved (one transaction checks all lines), the order becomes REJECTED_SHORT_STOCK with the short items listed, no payment is requested, and the cart is untouched.
sonnet.q3: The charge uses the order id as the idempotency key, and retries reuse the same key, so the provider does not charge twice. The payments row is also unique per order id.
sonnet.q4: Inventory replies out of stock and changes nothing. Order sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, emails the customer and publishes RefundRequested. Payment refunds the full amount, and Order emails the customer when RefundCompleted arrives. The cart is untouched.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only after the order is CONFIRMED (on OrderConfirmed); only the ordered lines are removed. On any failure (cart read failure, short stock, timeout, declined payment, out of stock) the cart is left exactly as it was.
sonnet.q6: No single orchestrator. Steps are driven by HTTP calls and events between services, plus recovery loops (the Order sweeper, Inventory expiry job, Payment reconciliation and refund loops). The record of progress is the order status in Order's orders table (with status_changed_at); Inventory and Payment keep their own reservation and payment statuses.
sonnet.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment (P2), which verifies the signature and updates the payment in P4. Payment then publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentFailed via its outbox and the broker. Order consumes it and finishes the order. The reconciliation job can also set the outcome by asking the provider.
sonnet.q8: Payment saves the provider event id in a unique-keyed table in the same transaction as the status change. A repeat collides and is ignored with a 200 reply. Status updates are conditional on still being REQUESTED. On the Order side, consumers decide by current status, so a repeat event is ignored.
sonnet.q9: The hold is released early. Payment publishes PaymentFailed, Order sets PAYMENT_DECLINED and publishes OrderFailed, and Inventory (I4) sets the reservation RELEASED and returns the stock to sale, but only if it is still RESERVED.
sonnet.q10: Order sets PAID_CLAIMING and asks Inventory to claim. If the hold is EXPIRED, Inventory checks in one transaction whether every line has available stock >= quantity. If yes, it deducts on_hand, sets CLAIMED and the order is fulfilled (CONFIRMED). If any line is short it changes nothing, and Order cancels as out of stock and requests a refund.
sonnet.q11: The refund row (saved before calling the provider, unique per order id) stays PENDING. The refund scheduler in Payment (about every minute) retries with backoff and the same refund key. After N failures the row becomes REFUND_FAILED and ops is alerted, but retries continue. The row is never deleted until it is REFUNDED. It is tracked in Payment's refunds table.
sonnet.q12: The Cart service does it. Order publishes OrderConfirmed (after the claim succeeds and the order is CONFIRMED), and Cart (K1) removes the ordered lines in one transaction guarded by applied_orders.
